solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Card cutter to double up (9)

blocks.note: the jack is a playing card
a knife cuts

annotation.surface: Someone cutting playing cards in half, or a card trick gone wrong.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Card cutter' reads as one thing, a tool for trimming card, but it splits into two words that simply sit side by side.
annotation.definitionFit: To jackknife is to fold double, like the blade of the pocket knife, as a diver or an articulated lorry does.

entries.clue: Music ringing so long on the phone before one[’s] bath (7)

indicatorNotes.ringing: to ring something is to encircle it, so JAZZ goes round CU
indicatorNotes.before: the letters for 'one' come right after the rest

blocks.note: a kind of music
text-message shorthand for 'see you', a goodbye
Roman numeral one

annotation.surface: Someone lingering on a phone call with music playing before getting into the bath.
annotation.walkthrough: 'On the phone' points to texting, where CU stands for 'see you', i.e. goodbye or so long. 'Ringing' looks like a telephone bell but is the instruction to surround.
annotation.definitionFit: A Jacuzzi is a whirlpool bath, the trade name used generally.

entries.clue: Cry when putting up with a cold (3)

indicatorNotes.putting up: in a down clue, putting letters up reads them bottom to top

blocks.note: W is short for with
the article as written
C for cold, as on a tap

annotation.surface: Complaining when you have to put up with a cold.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Putting up with' reads as one phrase meaning tolerating; split it, and 'putting up' reverses while 'with' is W.
annotation.definitionFit: A caw is the harsh cry of a crow or rook.

entries.clue: The King departs after broadcast [is] dubbed (8)

indicatorNotes.broadcast: to broadcast seed is to scatter it, so the letters are thrown about
indicatorNotes.after: D comes after the rearranged letters

blocks.note: THE KING rearranged
D is the timetable abbreviation for departs

annotation.surface: The King leaves after making a radio broadcast.
annotation.walkthrough: The royal picture fits the answer: a monarch dubs a knight with a sword. 'Broadcast' feels like radio but only scatters THE KING.
annotation.definitionFit: To dub someone is to make them a knight by touching their shoulder with a sword.

entries.clue: Turning 50, detective retired on being unwilling to work (5)

indicatorNotes.Turning: turning something round reverses it, so L DI becomes IDL
indicatorNotes.retired: to retire is to go back, so RE becomes ER

blocks.note: L is 50 in Roman numerals
Detective Inspector
RE means on or about, as in a memo

annotation.surface: A police detective turning fifty and retiring because he no longer wants to work.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Being' is a noun here, a creature or person, so the definition is a person unwilling to work. 'Retired on' reverses RE, which means on the subject of.
annotation.definitionFit: An idler is someone who avoids work, a being unwilling to work.

entries.clue: Cut out boxing casualty stateside with right training equipment (9)

indicatorNotes.boxing: to box something is to enclose it, so EXCISE holds ER
indicatorNotes.with: with means accompanied by, so R joins on at the end

blocks.note: to excise is to cut out
the emergency room, the American name for a hospital casualty department
R for right

annotation.surface: A boxer's injury in America stopping them using the gym kit.
annotation.walkthrough: Casualty is the British name for a hospital's emergency department; 'stateside' asks for the American version, ER. 'Boxing' sits in the sporting picture but means enclosing.
annotation.definitionFit: An exerciser is a machine or device for physical training.

entries.clue: Slide down off leaking old boat (5)

indicatorNotes.leaking: something that leaks loses its contents, so OFF loses O

blocks.note: to ski is to slide down a slope
the word as written
O for old, the letter that leaks away

annotation.surface: Sliding off a leaky old boat as it sinks.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Leaking old boat' seems to describe the definition; in fact 'leaking old' tells OFF to lose its O, and only 'boat' defines.
annotation.definitionFit: A skiff is a small light rowing or sailing boat.

entries.clue: Sell out second match with English going two down (6)

indicatorNotes.English going two down: E is English, and in a down entry going two down moves that E two places lower in the word

blocks.note: S for second
to match is to equal; its E, for English, then slides two places down

annotation.surface: A second match lost, with England's side two goals down.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Two down' sounds like a scoreline but is a literal instruction: in EQUAL the E slides down two places to give QUEAL.
annotation.definitionFit: To squeal is slang for informing on someone, betraying or selling them out.

entries.clue: Tending to mix vinaigrette in buffet (11)

indicatorNotes.buffet: to buffet is to knock about, so the letters are battered into a new order

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 11 letters

annotation.surface: Advice to toss the salad dressing through the dishes at a buffet.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Buffet' tempts as a spread of food, which suits the dressing, but it is the verb to batter. 'Mix' also sounds like an anagram signal and is only part of the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: Integrative means serving to combine parts into a whole, tending to mix.

entries.clue: Aid for delivery rider under duress (7)

indicatorNotes.under: in a down entry, PS goes below FORCE

blocks.note: duress is compulsion, force
a rider is an addition to a document, like a postscript

annotation.surface: A delivery driver being made to work under pressure.
annotation.walkthrough: The courier picture misleads twice: 'delivery' is childbirth and 'rider' is an added clause, the PS at the end of a letter.
annotation.definitionFit: Forceps are the tongs an obstetrician may use to help deliver a baby.

entries.clue: Lady driving cattle truck about to open bonnet (7)

indicatorNotes.about: turned about, so RIG reads GIR
indicatorNotes.to open: GIR splits COWL open by going inside it

blocks.note: a rig is a big truck, North American usage
a cowl is a hood, and also the bonnet over an engine

annotation.surface: A woman driving a cattle truck lifts the bonnet to look at the engine.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Cattle truck' reads as one vehicle, but 'cattle' belongs to the definition and 'truck' alone gives RIG. A bonnet is the British word for a car's hood.
annotation.definitionFit: A cowgirl is a woman who herds cattle on a ranch.

entries.clue: Adequate to shed a couple of layers to run — it’s a constant zero degrees (7)

indicatorNotes.shed a couple of layers: peeling off two outer layers removes the outside letters twice, A..E then D..T

blocks.note: ADEQUATE with two letters stripped from each end
the word as written
R for run, as in cricket scores

annotation.surface: Advice to take off a couple of layers to go running, since it's a constant temperature.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface suggests weather: zero degrees sounds freezing, yet the equator is famously hot. The degrees are of latitude, not temperature.
annotation.definitionFit: The equator is the line of latitude zero degrees, the same all the way round the globe.

entries.clue: Nothing in Brazil changes (5)

indicatorNotes.in: the answer sits inside the words that follow

blocks.note: the answer spans the end of Brazil and the start of changes

annotation.surface: A remark that nothing ever changes in Brazil.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Changes' looks like an anagram signal, but no rearranging is needed; the letters run straight across the word break.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym in American slang: zero, zip, not a thing.

entries.clue: Regularly-screened live reality reels bringing in capital with profit (11)

indicatorNotes.Regularly-screened: every other letter of LIVE is screened off, hidden, leaving LV
indicatorNotes.reels: to reel is to stagger about, so the letters are jumbled
indicatorNotes.bringing in: the jumbled letters take UC inside

blocks.note: L(i)V(e), the second and fourth letters hidden
the word as written, jumbled with LV
capital letters are upper case, UC

annotation.surface: A regular live reality TV show pulling in viewers and money.
annotation.walkthrough: The TV words 'screened', 'live', 'reality' and 'reels' make a surface about television; each has another job. UC for upper case is the shorthand behind 'capital'.
annotation.definitionFit: Lucratively means in a way that brings in money, with profit.

entries.clue: Ravel again occupied by concerto’s opening figure (9)

indicatorNotes.occupied by: RETANGLE is occupied, so C goes inside it
indicatorNotes.opening: the opening of a word is its first letter

blocks.note: to ravel is to tangle, so ravel again is re-tangle
first letter of concerto

annotation.surface: A concerto by the composer Ravel played again, starting with its opening.
annotation.walkthrough: Ravel with a capital is the French composer, and the concerto keeps up the musical picture; here it is the ordinary verb ravel, to tangle.
annotation.definitionFit: A rectangle is a geometric figure with four right angles.

entries.clue: Swells are contracted to wear fashionable suits? (9)

indicatorNotes.contracted: a contraction shortens a word, so 'are' becomes 'RE, as in we're
indicatorNotes.to wear: clothes surround the wearer, so CASES goes round RE

blocks.note: in fashion
the short form of are, as in they're
lawsuits are cases

annotation.surface: Toffs who have signed up to wear trendy suits.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Swells' at the start looks like a noun for smart dressers, which the fashionable suits encourage, but it is the verb, grows. The question mark flags suits as lawsuits.
annotation.definitionFit: To swell is to grow larger, to increase.

entries.clue: Crack user with speed set aside (9)

indicatorNotes.Crack: a cracked thing breaks up, so the letters fall apart and are reassembled

blocks.note: anagram fodder
anagram fodder

annotation.surface: A crack cocaine user who has given up speed, the amphetamine.
annotation.walkthrough: The drug picture uses crack and speed, but 'Crack' is the instruction and speed is just five letters of fodder.
annotation.definitionFit: To supersede something is to replace it, setting it aside for something newer.

entries.clue: Hamburgers’ rather depleted buns [in] boxes (4)

indicatorNotes.depleted: emptied, so BUNS loses its inner letters

blocks.note: German for yes; 'rather!' is an old British way of saying yes
B(un)S with the middle emptied out

annotation.surface: A fast-food complaint: the hamburgers' buns are rather thin.
annotation.walkthrough: Hamburgers are people from Hamburg, so their 'rather', meaning yes indeed, is German JA. Boxes is the verb, to punch.
annotation.definitionFit: To jab is to throw short punches, as a boxer does.

entries.clue: Fourteen points for Piquet [and] reportedly Jaguar with eight? (8)

indicatorNotes.reportedly: as reported, spoken, so the sound is what counts

blocks.note: a jaguar is a cat; a rowing eight has eight oars

annotation.surface: A card game question mixed with a Jaguar car and eight cylinders.
annotation.walkthrough: Piquet is an old two-player card game in which four of a kind scores fourteen points, a quatorze. The question mark covers eight standing for its oars.
annotation.definitionFit: In piquet a quatorze is a set of four aces, kings, queens, jacks or tens, worth fourteen points.

entries.clue: Influence introduction of welfare state checks (4)

indicatorNotes.introduction of: the introduction of a word is its first letter
indicatorNotes.checks: to check is to hold back, so SAY holds W

blocks.note: to state is to say
first letter of welfare

annotation.surface: The welfare state's checks, from its beginning, carrying influence.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Welfare state' reads as one phrase; split it, and state is SAY while only the W of welfare is used.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to hold sway over people is to have power over them.

entries.clue: Field reserve clubs wearing black (7)

indicatorNotes.wearing: clubs is worn by black, so JET goes round C

blocks.note: a reserve player is a substitute, a sub
jet black
C for clubs, the card suit

annotation.surface: A reserve golfer out on the field with his clubs, dressed in black.
annotation.walkthrough: The sports words are all misdirection: 'Field' is an area of study, and clubs is the card suit's C.
annotation.definitionFit: A field of study, such as history or physics, is a subject.

entries.clue: One spiked long drinks in gold vessel (9)

indicatorNotes.drinks in: to drink something in is to take it inside, so PINE holds OR CUP

blocks.note: to long for is to pine
OR is gold in heraldry
a cup is a drinking vessel

annotation.surface: Someone whose long drinks were spiked in a golden goblet.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Spiked' and 'long drinks' paint doctored cocktails; the spikes are quills and 'long' is the verb to pine.
annotation.definitionFit: A porcupine is an animal covered with sharp spines, a spiked one.

entries.clue: Fellow feeling extremely happy after lunch drinks served up past noon (7)

indicatorNotes.extremely: only the extreme, outermost letters of happy are used
indicatorNotes.after: after means following in order, so the letters from happy come last
indicatorNotes.drinks: EAT drinks, takes in, the reversed PM
indicatorNotes.served up: in a down entry, served up reads bottom to top, so PM becomes MP

blocks.note: to lunch is to eat
post meridiem, after midday
H(app)Y, its outer letters

annotation.surface: A friend feeling very merry after a lunch where drinks went on past midday.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is a boozy long lunch, but 'drinks' is a container instruction and 'served up' a reversal; nothing here is about alcohol.
annotation.definitionFit: Empathy is fellow feeling, sharing another person's emotions.

entries.clue: Jolly permissive parts [for] array of stars (6)

indicatorNotes.parts: LAX parts GAY, splitting it to sit in the middle

blocks.note: gay in its older sense, merry
lax rules are permissive

annotation.surface: Cheerful, easygoing roles in a film for a cast full of stars.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Parts' looks like a noun, roles in a show, fitting the star-studded picture; it is the verb, LAX dividing GAY.
annotation.definitionFit: A galaxy is a vast system of stars, and figuratively any brilliant assembly.

entries.clue: Antiques — British Isles to return a couple shortly (4-1-4)

indicatorNotes.to return: going back reverses CI to IC
indicatorNotes.shortly: cut short, so BRACE loses its last letter

blocks.note: BR for British
the Channel Islands, CI
the article as written
a brace is a pair, cut short

annotation.surface: Antiques from the British Isles coming home as a pair.
annotation.walkthrough: 'British Isles' reads as one place; it is BR plus CI, the Channel Islands off the French coast. A brace means two, used of game birds.
annotation.definitionFit: Bric-a-brac is a jumble of small old ornaments and curios.

entries.clue: Munch hot party sandwiches (5)

indicatorNotes.sandwiches: a sandwich holds its filling, so CAMP holds H

blocks.note: a camp is a faction, a party within a group
H for hot, as on a tap

annotation.surface: Guests at a party eating hot sandwiches.
annotation.walkthrough: Sandwiches and munching make a party-food picture; 'sandwiches' is the verb to enclose.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: horses champ at the bit, chewing noisily, as in champing at the bit.

entries.clue: Charlie[’s] parking by Barbican perhaps after pulling over (5)

indicatorNotes.after pulling over: once O for over is pulled out, TOWER is left as TWER
indicatorNotes.by: by means next to, so the P for parking stands right beside the rest

blocks.note: a barbican is a gate tower; 'perhaps' marks it as one example
O for over, as in cricket scoring
P for parking, as on road signs

annotation.surface: A man called Charlie parking near the Barbican in London after being pulled over by police.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Charlie' is British slang for a fool, not a name. The Barbican is a London arts centre, but a barbican is also a fortified gate tower.
annotation.definitionFit: A twerp is a silly person, which is what a charlie is in British slang.

entries.clue: Give a lift to visiting French student nurses (7)

indicatorNotes.nurses: to nurse is to hold close, so ELEVE holds AT

blocks.note: visiting somewhere, you are at it
élève is French for pupil

annotation.surface: Nurses offering a lift to a visiting French student.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Nurses' looks like the people giving the lift; it is the verb, to cradle.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to raise someone up, in position or rank, is to give them a lift.

entries.clue: Pop round to get cheese, forgetting ‘thank you’ [for] fruit (7)

indicatorNotes.forgetting: leaving out, so RICOTTA drops TA

blocks.note: pop and pa both mean father
an Italian soft cheese
ta is British informal for thanks

annotation.surface: Dad popping round to fetch cheese and forgetting to say thanks.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Pop round' is a British phrase for a quick visit; split, 'Pop' is father and 'round' turns him about.
annotation.definitionFit: An apricot is a small orange stone fruit.

entries.clue: Chief of Staff / leaves / function (3)

blocks.note: the abbreviation
a variety of lettuce with long crisp leaves, called romaine in America
the abbreviated name of a trigonometric function

annotation.walkthrough: This is a triple definition, marked off by the slashes. Cos lettuce is the British name for romaine.
annotation.definitionFit: COS abbreviates Chief of Staff, names a lettuce, and is the cosine function in trigonometry.

entries.clue: Your old dear [is] like Herb (5)

blocks.note: thy is the old form of your
'my!' and 'dear!' are both mild exclamations of surprise

annotation.surface: An old-fashioned endearment for someone called Herb.
annotation.walkthrough: The capital H makes Herb look like a man's name; it is the plant, here thyme.
annotation.definitionFit: Thymy means like or smelling of thyme, a herb.

entries.clue: Former president scheming with specific intent (9)

blocks.note: an ex is a former partner
short for president
sly and scheming both mean crafty

annotation.surface: A former president plotting with a clear purpose.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Former president' reads as one person; it breaks into EX and PRES.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: an instruction given expressly is stated plainly for one particular purpose.
